svg.title: Ku-band radio receiver signal chain
svg.desc: Complete signal chain from 10.7–12.75 GHz Ku-band sky signal through LNB downconversion, bias tee, 1420 MHz bandpass filter, LNA, mixer to 10 MHz IF, second bandpass filter, amplifier, AD790JN comparator 1-bit digitisation, Shrike Lite FPGA XNOR correlator, and RP2040 23-bit counter to USB serial PC output.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What is the Ku-band frequency range and how does it get received from a satellite?')
sendPrompt('Explain how the Ku-band LNB works — dual LO bands, gain, and noise figure')
sendPrompt('What does the bias tee do and why is 12 V fed up the coax to the LNB?')
sendPrompt('Why is there a bandpass filter centred at 1420 MHz — what is the significance of that frequency?')
sendPrompt('What is the purpose of the LNA after the bandpass filter, and what noise figure would be typical?')
sendPrompt('Explain the mixing stage: 1420 MHz signal mixed with 1410 MHz LO produces 10 MHz IF')
sendPrompt('What is the role of the 10 MHz bandpass filter and why use ~2 MHz bandwidth?')
sendPrompt('What does the post-filter amplifier stage do before the comparator?')
sendPrompt('How does the AD790JN precision comparator convert the 10 MHz analog IF to a 1-bit digital signal?')
sendPrompt('How does the XNOR correlator in the Shrike Lite FPGA work for 1-bit radio astronomy correlation?')
sendPrompt('How does the RP2040 implement the 23-bit counter and stream data over USB serial to the PC?')
